# S123 — Warn in verify when the render merge driver is not configured

**Findings:**  · **Size:**  · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

The `slicer-generated` render merge driver (S109) only works after each clone runs a per-clone git config. S118 (`init` prints it) and S121 (`slicer setup-git`) surface the setup, but nothing detects when it has been forgotten -- you only find out when a merge writes conflict markers into `render/`, which happened on essentially every merge during recent parallel-worktree work. A warn-only finding in `slicer verify`, pointing at `slicer setup-git`, catches it once. `slicer check` is the git-free CI gate (`check.run` composes only `verify.offline`), so this git-querying check lives in `verify` (the git-aware command); the honest limitation is it surfaces on `verify`, not `check`.

## Files

- `src/slicer/vcs.py` -- add `("--get", "merge.slicer-generated.driver")` to `READ_ONLY["config"]`, and a read-only `render_driver_configured(root) -> bool` (mirrors the inline `config --get` in `identity`).
- `src/slicer/verify.py` -- in `against_git`, before the `git_check` early-return, when the root is a git repo and the driver is not configured, append `Finding("warn", "", ...)` pointing at `slicer setup-git`.
- tests (reuse the `tests/test_merge.py` pattern that runs `git config merge.slicer-generated.*`).
- docs: a line in `docs/getting-started.md` / `docs/agents.md`; a CHANGELOG entry.

## Failing tests

1. In a git repo with the driver not configured, `slicer verify` emits a warn-level finding naming `slicer setup-git`, and exits 0 (a warning never fails).
2. With the driver configured, no such warning.
3. Outside a git repo, no warning and no crash.
4. With `git_check` off, the driver warning still appears (it is independent of the history cross-check), while the done-but-uncommitted cross-check is skipped.
5. The vcs allowlist permits `git config --get merge.slicer-generated.driver` (read-only) and still refuses any config write.

## Implement

Allowlist the one read-only `config --get`; add `vcs.render_driver_configured`; in `verify.against_git`, gated on `is_repo` and independent of `git_check`, append a warn Finding when the driver is not configured, pointing at `slicer setup-git`. Do not touch `check.run` -- it stays git-free. The driver name `merge.slicer-generated.driver` is a bare literal in `cli.py` today; reuse the literal here and optionally note a future shared constant, but do not refactor it in this slice.

Product decisions settled: the warning is independent of `git_check` (it is about this clone's setup, not history); there is no config opt-out for a project that deliberately skips the driver (deferred) -- every project gets the driver in `.gitattributes` from `init`, so a not-configured clone is the real gap.

## Check

The five cases above pass. `slicer check` and the unit suite pass.
